recognize_zh: 這是 G 顯帶核型圖（karyogram）而非形態學影像：2 條 X、無 Y，第 1 對與第 9 對染色體被圈起，其中一條 1 號與一條 9 號長度與帶型與同源染色體不同，代表 t(1;9)(p13;p12) 平衡易位。
features: G-banded karyogram of a female metaphase (two X chromosomes, no Y)
Chromosome 1 pair circled: one homolog shows an altered short arm banding pattern and length
Chromosome 9 pair circled: one homolog shows altered short arm material, indicating the reciprocal partner
Remaining autosomes show 22 normal-appearing pairs; no marker chromosome in the mar slot
Banding resolution is modest, so exact breakpoints cannot be confirmed from the image alone
describe_en: This figure is a G-banded karyogram rather than a morphologic image. It shows a female karyotype with 46 chromosomes in which one chromosome 1 and one chromosome 9 (both circled) display altered short-arm banding consistent with a reciprocal translocation, while the other chromosomes appear structurally normal. Given the modest banding resolution, the breakpoints are best reported with uncertainty, as 46,XX,t(1;9)(p?13;p?12). In the clinical context of CD19+/CD10+ B-lymphoblastic leukemia negative for common recurrent fusions, this is an uncommon sole abnormality; the 9p12 region includes PAX5, which could be evaluated by FISH or molecular testing.

ddx.vs: The recurrent t(1;19) involves 1q23 and 19p13 rather than 1p and 9p, and TCF3::PBX1 was negative by PCR in this case.
The Philadelphia translocation affects 9q34 and produces a shortened chromosome 22, which is not seen here.
9p deletions produce loss of material without a reciprocal partner on chromosome 1, so FISH or genomic studies are needed to distinguish them from a balanced translocation.
